MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: # Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: the same three coordinate ranges.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: 445--480, paper lines 970--989.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean: /-- An extended line is compatible with two source lines as soon as each of

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: # Coordinate blocks of a truncated extended direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: vector by zeroing the coordinates that precede the stored coordinate index,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: so each source block is again a prefix truncation: when the stored index is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: preceding blocks vanish, and later blocks remain untruncated.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean: two identified scalar fields.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: # Products and push-forwards of finite distributions
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma presents one law both as an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: independent product of its generating blocks and as a dependent mixture over
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: one of those blocks.  This module records the three rewriting rules that pass
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: between the two presentations: a push-forward of the first factor of a product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: is a push-forward of the product, a product with a probability law in the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: second factor has the first factor as its marginal, and a push-forward of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: product is the dependent mixture of the push-forwards of its second factor.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: The product and mixture operations are those of blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `def:line-point-dist`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-! ## Nonemptiness of the support of a probability law -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-- A law of total mass one has a nonempty support.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-! ## Push-forward of one factor of a product -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-- Pushing the first factor of a product forward is pushing the product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: forward along the map acting on that factor alone.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-! ## The first marginal of a product -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-- The first marginal of a product whose second factor is a probability law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: is the first factor.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-- Reading a function of the first factor of a product whose second factor is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: a probability law is reading it on the first factor.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-! ## A product as a dependent mixture -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: /-- A push-forward of a product is the dependent mixture, over the first
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: factor, of the push-forwards of the second factor.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: # The two independent blocks of a fresh diagonal direction pair
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: This module splits the fresh diagonal direction pair of the sub-line sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: procedure into its two independent blocks.  The coordinate-index event
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: constrains only the scalar seed of the pair, so conditioning on it leaves the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: direction block uniform and independent of the conditioned seed.  The
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: direction block of a fresh pair is therefore available as an unconstrained
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: uniform vector, which is what allows the sampling procedure to read it off the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: corresponding block of the direction of the sampled extended line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: The block decomposition supports `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: The coordinate-index event is that of `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: lines 1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-! ## Conditioning the first factor of a product -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-- Restricting a product law to an event depending on the first factor alone
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: leaves the second factor unchanged and independent of the conditioned first
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: factor.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the mass of an event depending only on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: first factor is the same under a uniform product law and under the uniform
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: law of that factor.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-- Conditioning a uniform product law on an event of its first factor leaves

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-! ## The coordinate-index event on a scalar seed -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineSeed.lean: /-- The coordinate-index event of `def:ith-restricted-line` read on a scalar

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: # Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean: same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: # Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: procedure of the sub-line lemma. First, for independent uniform inputs `y` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: the ambient coordinate space and `t` in the scalar field, the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `lineRepMap v y + t • v` is uniform. This map on ambient-point--parameter pairs
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: has fibers of size `q`: for nonzero `v`, `y` varies over a coset of the span of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `v`, while its canonical representative and `t` are fixed; for zero `v`, `y`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: is fixed and `t` is free. Second, the two coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: coordinates.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: The canonical representative map is blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: blueprint `def:combine-map`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: /-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: /-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: # The ordered point product on a single placement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: triangle inequality twice.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: `Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: /-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: between the two members of each pair. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: /-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean: `Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: # Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: is not itself a measurement.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: step at paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: the square root of the line effect, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: two diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The averaged form of the preceding estimate: the average over a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: distribution of the outcome sums of `Re ⟨u, A v⟩` is bounded by the product of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: the square roots of the two averaged diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-! ## Quadratic forms against projections -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The real quadratic form is invariant under the conjugate transpose. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Conjugating an operator transfers the outer operator to the state vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- For a projection `B` commuting with `A`, the quadratic form of `A` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `B ψ` is the quadratic form of `A B` in `ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The quadratic form of an operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: the squared norm of the vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The effects of a complete measurement have total quadratic form one on a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: unit vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Weighting a complete measurement by commuting projections cannot exceed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: the total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-! ## Replacing a factor under the weight of a measurement -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Cauchy--Schwarz with the measurement as weight: for projections `B`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: commuting with the effects of `A`, the averaged overlap of `A` against the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: product `B C` is bounded by the square roots of the averaged overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: against `B` and of the averaged quadratic form of `A` in `C ψ`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: Cauchy--Schwarz step of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate: for projections `B` and `C`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: commuting with the effects of `A`, replacing the factor `C B` by `C` inside an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: overlap weighted by the complete measurement `A` changes the average by at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: most the square root of the deficit `1 - E Σ_a ⟨A_a B_a⟩`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: estimate used in the proof of `lem:claim-17-2` and, with `C = Id`, in the proof
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate with the product family
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `C B` supplied as one family `CB`, which is convenient when the product is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: formed on a local space before being placed. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- Inserting an arbitrary operator family `W` after a projection family `R`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: commuting with the effects of `A` costs at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: averaged squared norms of `W ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: /-- The mirror image of the preceding estimate: an operator family `W`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: commuting with the effects of `A`, inserted before a commuting projection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: family `R`, costs at most the square root of the averaged squared norms of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean: `Wᴴ ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: # Placement calculus on the expanded state
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1003-1030`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.  The
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: EPR-exchange invariance is the element `U_σ U_θ` of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1032-1130`, which needs no
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: symmetry of the strategy; its use for `lem:qld-4-10` is analyzed in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-! ## The placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: space. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement preserves positivity. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The placement of a local operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: the identity. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- The placement of a projector is a contraction. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- Operators placed on opposite register pairs commute. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A complete measurement on a local expanded space, placed on one of the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placed projective measurement is projective. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean: /-- A placement maps the zero operator to zero. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: # Sub-line averages of the Z-point overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: The overlap of the paired-line measurement with the expanded `Z`-point effect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: depends only on the two source lines and the `Z`-point. The separate Z marginal
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: of the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` law is a mixture of products of restricted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: line-point laws, with the fresh X point unused. Summing line answers over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: evaluation fibers at that fresh point identifies the overlap with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: evaluated pair-line overlap, so the Z deficit estimates of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ZEvalDeficit` apply component by component.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: The `_at` estimates and `zPointOverlapAt` retain arbitrary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: opposite placements. The original overlap definitions and first-player
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: statements are unchanged. Only the separate Z marginal mixture law is used.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: Transport of the auxiliary extended-line law to the source carrier remains
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: open; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean: "Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: # A uniform point of the extended space from the directly indexed sub-line law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: from the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points. These
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: identities concern `directLinePointDist`. Transport to the source's seed-indexed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: carrier remains open, as recorded in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: "Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: These statements support `lem:claim-17-1` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  The paper uses this sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: fact at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1159-1166`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- A dependent mixture of a constant family is the constant law. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- If every slice of a map of a pair carries the second uniform law to one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: fixed law, then the map carries the uniform law of the pair to that law. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Apply the shared uniform-point identity to an ambient point and an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: independent affine parameter. This preserves the existing public name for the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: identity supplied by `uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Reading a point at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: uniform direct sample gives a uniform point of the direct coordinate space. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Averaging a function at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: of a uniform direct sample is averaging it at a uniform point. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- A uniform point on a line drawn from the directly indexed line-point law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: is uniform in the ambient coordinate space. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Identify the directly indexed extended coordinates with the combining
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: coordinate split. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Split an extended point into its two source blocks and two remaining
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: scalar coordinates. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- The two source blocks of a uniform extended point are independent and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: uniform after the canonical scalar identification. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: /-- Under a sub-line witness, the two source blocks of the point at a uniform
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean: affine parameter are independent uniform source points. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: # Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The proof of `lem:claim-17-3` bounds, after its Cauchy--Schwarz step, the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: deficit of the overlap between the evaluated pair-line measurement and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: expanded `Z`-point measurement at the `Z`-point of the sample.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: This module derives that deficit from the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: consistency of the evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: point measurement and from the closeness of the joint point measurement to the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: ordered point products. The derivation inserts the joint point measurement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: on the point side, replaces it by the ordered product whose trailing factor is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the retained point effect, and sums the other factor, at the cost of three
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: square roots. The deficit is first bounded over an arbitrary probability
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of two restricted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The `_at` variants retain arbitrary opposite placements, including Bob at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `BBprime` and Alice at `ABdoubleprime`. The original statements are unchanged
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: specializations; register commutation does not assume symmetry of the state.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: ## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: The Z deficit is the quantity bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `lem:qld-4-10`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## Completed point pairs -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: evaluations. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the completion. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A placed projection is a projection. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- Every effect of the completed expanded point measurement is a projection,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the `none` effect being zero. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed joint point measurement and a completed point product differ
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- The completed `Z`-then-`X` point product vanishes on both `none` classes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: and restricts to the ordered product on evaluated pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-! ## The two placed deficits -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean: /-- A pair of line-point pairs of the source space: the sample type of the

/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a

within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`

Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind

        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a))| ≤
      Real.sqrt η := by
    have hpt : ∀ x,

        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((1 - (Q x).effect a) * R x a)) := by
      intro x
      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, sub_mul, mul_sub]
    rw [abs_sub_comm, ← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]

  have h5' := abs_le.mp h5

   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   208	    (μ : Distribution X) (A Q : X → Measurement α ι) (R W : X → α → Op ι)
   209	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   210	    (hQ : ∀ x, Measurement.IsProjective (Q x)) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
   211	    (hAQ : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((Q x).effect a))
   212	    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a))
   213	    (hAW : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a))
   214	    (hWR : ∀ x a, W x a * R x a = W x a)
   215	    (hnonneg : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a))
   216	    (η ζ : ℝ)
   217	    (hcons : consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
   218	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ ≤ η)
   219	    (hdist : opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (Q x).effect a)
   220	      (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ ≤ ζ) :
   221	    1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) ≤
   222	      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
   223	  set ovQ := avgOver μ (fun x =>
   224	    ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a)) with hovQ
   225	  have h1 : 1 - ovQ ≤ η := by
   226	    rw [← consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ A Q ψ hμ hψ]
   227	    exact hcons
   228	  have hovQ_nonneg : 0 ≤ ovQ :=
   229	    avgOver_nonneg μ _ fun x => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => hnonneg x a
   230	  have hovQ_le : ovQ ≤ 1 :=
   231	    avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ hμ hψ
   232	      (fun x a => hQ x a) hAQ
   233	  have h1' : 1 - ovQ ≤ Real.sqrt η := by
   234	    have h0 : 0 ≤ 1 - ovQ := by linarith
   235	    calc 1 - ovQ = Real.sqrt ((1 - ovQ) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq h0).symm
   236	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (by nlinarith)
   237	  -- comparing `Q` with `W` under the weight `A`
   238	  have hWconj : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a) =
   239	      stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a)ᴴ) := by
   240	    intro x a
   241	    rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a),
   242	      Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, measurement_effect_hermitian]
   243	    congr 1
   244	    have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (hAW x a).eq
   245	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
   246	      measurement_effect_hermitian] at h
   247	    exact h
   248	  have h2 : |ovQ - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   249	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤ Real.sqrt ζ := by
   250	    rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hWconj x a]
   251	    exact abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq μ A
   252	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ hμ hψ ζ hdist
   253	  -- replacing `Q R` by `W R = W`
   254	  have h4 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   255	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   256	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤
   257	      Real.sqrt ζ := by
   258	    have hpt : ∀ x,
   259	        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   260	          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a)) =
   261	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (((Q x).effect a - W x a) * R x a)) := by
   262	      intro x
   263	      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   264	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   265	      rw [sub_mul, hWR]
   266	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   267	    rw [← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
   268	    have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj' μ A
   269	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a - W x a) R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
   270	      (fun x a => (hAQ x a).sub_right (hAW x a))
   271	    refine hcs.trans (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ?_)
   272	    have hdist' : avgOver μ (fun x =>
   273	        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState ((Q x).effect a - (W x a)ᴴ) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤ ζ :=
   274	      hdist
   275	    refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ hdist'
   276	    refine avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   277	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, measurement_effect_hermitian]
   278	  -- inserting `Q` before `R`
   279	  have h5 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   280	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   281	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a))| ≤
   282	      Real.sqrt η := by
   283	    have hpt : ∀ x,
   284	        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) -
   285	          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) =
   286	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((1 - (Q x).effect a) * R x a)) := by
   287	      intro x
   288	      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   289	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   290	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, sub_mul, mul_sub]
   291	    rw [abs_sub_comm, ← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
   292	    have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ A
   293	      (fun x a => 1 - (Q x).effect a) R ψ (fun x a => (hQ x a).one_sub)
   294	      (fun x a => (Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAQ x a))
   295	    have hfirst : avgOver μ (fun x =>
   296	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - (Q x).effect a))) = 1 - ovQ := by
   297	      have hx : ∀ x,
   298	          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - (Q x).effect a))) =
   299	            1 - ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a) := by
   300	        intro x
   301	        rw [← sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   302	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   303	        simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   304	      rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ hx, avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ]
   305	    have hsecond : avgOver μ (fun x =>
   306	        ∑ a, stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (R x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a)) ≤ 1 := by
   307	      rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
   308	        stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (hR x a) (hAR x a)]
   309	      exact avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
   310	    rw [hfirst] at hcs
   311	    calc
   312	      _ ≤ _ := hcs
   313	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - ovQ) * 1 := by
   314	        refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   315	        rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
   316	        exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hsecond
   317	      _ = Real.sqrt (1 - ovQ) := mul_one _
   318	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h1
   319	  have h2' := abs_le.mp h2
   320	  have h4' := abs_le.mp h4
   321	  have h5' := abs_le.mp h5
   322	  linarith [h2'.1, h4'.1, h5'.1, h2'.2, h4'.2, h5'.2]

   326	/-- A pair of line-point pairs of the source space: the sample type of the
   327	consistency display of `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
   328	abbrev LinePointPairSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   329	  (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) ×
   330	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))

   332	section Placed

   334	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}

   337	/-- The `Z`-point deficit of the evaluated pair-line measurement over a
   338	probability law on pairs of line-point pairs, from the consistency of the
   339	evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint point measurement
   340	and the closeness of the latter to the `Z`-then-`X` product.  This is the
   341	deficit bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
   342	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
   343	theorem CombinedLinesWitness.one_sub_Z_overlap_le_at
   344	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
   345	    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second)
   346	    (ν : Distribution (LinePointPairSample P)) (hν : ν.IsProbability) (η ζ : ℝ)
   347	    (hcons : consistencyDefect ν
   348	      (fun s o => S.place first
   349	        (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   350	          (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o))
   351	      (fun s o => S.place second
   352	        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   353	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
   354	      S.psiHat ≤ η)
   355	    (hZX : opFamilyDistSq ν
   356	      (fun s o => S.place second
   357	        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   358	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
   359	      (fun s o => S.place second
   360	        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
   361	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1))
   362	      S.psiHat ≤ ζ) :
   363	    1 - avgOver ν (fun s =>
   364	      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   365	        stateQForm S.psiHat
   366	          (S.place first
   367	            (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   368	              (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
   369	            S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))) ≤
   370	      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
   371	  have hQproj : ∀ s : LinePointPairSample P,
   372	      Measurement.IsProjective (S.placedMeasurement second
   373	        ((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2))) :=
   374	    fun s => S.placedMeasurement_isProjective _ _
   375	      (completedPair_isProjective _ (points.projective _ _ _))
   376	  have hRproj : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
   377	      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
   378	      IsProj (S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2)) :=
   379	    fun s o => S.place_isProj _ (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj _ _ _ _)
   380	  have hWR : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
   381	      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
   382	      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   383	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) *
   384	        S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) =
   385	      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   386	        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) := by
   387	    intro s o
   388	    have hlocal : (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   389	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
   390	        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 =
   391	        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   392	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 := by
   393	      rw [mul_assoc, (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .Z s.2.2 o.2).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   394	    exact (ProjectiveSetting.place_mul S second _ _).symm.trans
   395	      (congrArg (S.place second) hlocal)
   396	  have hnonneg : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
   397	      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
   398	      0 ≤ stateQForm S.psiHat
   399	        (S.place first
   400	          (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   401	            (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
   402	          S.place second
   403	            (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   404	              (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o)) :=
   405	    fun s o => stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg first second hopposite
   406	      (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   407	        (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).pos o)
   408	      (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   409	        (some ab.1, some ab.2)).pos o))
   410	  have hdist : opFamilyDistSq ν
   411	      (fun s o => S.place second
   412	        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   413	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
   414	      (fun s o => (S.place second
   415	        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   416	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))ᴴ)
   417	      S.psiHat ≤ ζ := by
   418	    refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ hZX
   419	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   420	    refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun s => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ => ?_
   421	    have hlocal : ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   422	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2)ᴴ =
   423	        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
   424	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 := by
   425	      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
   426	        (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .Z s.2.2 o.2).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   427	        (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .X s.1.2 o.1).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   428	    have hplace : (S.place second
   429	        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   430	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))ᴴ =
   431	        S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
   432	          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1) :=
   433	      (ProjectiveSetting.place_conjTranspose S second _).symm.trans
   434	        (congrArg (S.place second) hlocal)
   435	    dsimp only
   436	    rw [hplace]
   437	  exact one_sub_overlap_le_of_consistencyDefect ν
   438	    (fun s => S.placedMeasurement first
   439	      ((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   440	        (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)))
   441	    (fun s => S.placedMeasurement second
   442	      ((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)))
   443	    (fun s o => S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))
   444	    (fun s o => S.place second
   445	      ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
   446	        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))
   447	    S.psiHat hν S.psiHat_norm hQproj hRproj
   448	    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
   449	    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
   450	    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
   451	    hWR hnonneg η ζ hcons hdist

   455	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
   456	    (ν : Distribution (LinePointPairSample P)) (hν : ν.IsProbability) (η ζ : ℝ)
   457	    (hcons : consistencyDefect ν
   458	      (fun s o => S.place .AA'

   460	          (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o))

   462	        (((points.Q .bob s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>

   465	    (hZX : opFamilyDistSq ν
   466	      (fun s o => S.place .BA''
   467	        (((points.Q .bob s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   468	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
   469	      (fun s o => S.place .BA''
   470	        ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
   471	          (S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .X s.1.2).effect o.1))
   472	      S.psiHat ≤ ζ) :
   473	    1 - avgOver ν (fun s =>
   474	      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   475	        stateQForm S.psiHat
   476	          (S.place .AA'
   477	            (((lines.T .alice s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   478	              (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
   479	            S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))) ≤

   481	  exact lines.one_sub_Z_overlap_le_at .AA' .BA'' trivial ν hν η ζ hcons hZX

   488	/-- Every restricted line-point law has total mass one. -/
   489	theorem restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams)
   490	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   491	    (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i).IsProbability := by
   492	  cases kind
   493	  · change (restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i).IsProbability
   494	    exact restrictedALineDist_isProbability P.toLdParams i
   495	  · change (restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i).IsProbability
   496	    exact restrictedDLineDist_isProbability P.toLdParams i

   498	/-- The point marginal of a restricted line-point law is uniform. -/
   499	theorem restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   500	    (i : Fin P.m) :
   501	    (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i).map Prod.snd =
   502	      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) := by
   503	  rw [restrictedLinePointDist_eq_map_prod, Distribution.map_map]
   504	  exact Distribution.prod_map_fst _ _ (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _
   505	    (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P i) (uniformDistribution_isProbability _))

   507	/-- The pair of points of a product of two restricted line-point laws is a
   508	uniform pair. -/
   509	theorem prod_restrictedLinePointDist_map_points (P : AdmissibleParams)
   510	    (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
   511	    (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
   512	        (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j)).map (fun s => (s.1.2, s.2.2)) =
   513	      uniformDistribution
   514	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   515	  have h : Distribution.prod ((restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i).map Prod.snd)
   516	      ((restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j).map Prod.snd) =
   517	      uniformDistribution
   518	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   519	    rw [restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd, restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd,
   520	      uniformDistribution_prod]
   521	  rw [← h, Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.prod_map_right,
   522	    Distribution.map_map]
   523	
   524	/-- A state-dependent distance between two families depending on the pair of
   525	points only, averaged over a product of two restricted line-point laws, is the
   526	distance averaged over a uniform pair of points. -/
   527	theorem opFamilyDistSq_prod_restricted_points {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   528	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (P : AdmissibleParams) (kindX kindZ : LineKind)
   529	    (i j : Fin P.m)
   530	    (F G : (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → α → Op ι)
   531	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   532	    opFamilyDistSq
   533	        (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
   534	          (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j))
   535	        (fun s a => F (s.1.2, s.2.2) a) (fun s a => G (s.1.2, s.2.2) a) ψ =
   536	      opFamilyDistSq
   537	        (uniformDistribution
   538	          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) F G ψ := by
   539	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   540	  rw [← prod_restrictedLinePointDist_map_points P kindX kindZ i j,
   541	    Distribution.avgOver_map]

   548	/-- The `Z`-point deficit over a product of two restricted line-point laws,
   549	with the inflation `4 m ^ 2` of the line consistency error and the inflation

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.UniformLinePoint

/-!
# Sub-line averages of the Z-point overlap

The overlap of the paired-line measurement with the expanded `Z`-point effect
depends only on the two source lines and the `Z`-point. The separate Z marginal
of the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` law is a mixture of products of restricted
line-point laws, with the fresh X point unused. Summing line answers over the
evaluation fibers at that fresh point identifies the overlap with the
evaluated pair-line overlap, so the Z deficit estimates of
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ZEvalDeficit` apply component by component.

The `_at` estimates and `zPointOverlapAt` retain arbitrary
opposite placements. The original overlap definitions and first-player
statements are unchanged. Only the separate Z marginal mixture law is used.
Transport of the auxiliary extended-line law to the source carrier remains
open; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
"Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".

## References

The statements support the auxiliary `lem:claim-17-3-direct-real`, near
the source `lem:claim-17-3` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
mixture is Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

noncomputable section

/-! ## Regrouping the line answers by their evaluations -/

/-- Summing a paired-line answer against a family of point effects that
depends on the answer only through its two evaluations is summing the
evaluation classes of the paired-line measurement against that family.  This
is the fiber regrouping of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-1`, `lem:claim-17-2`,
and `lem:claim-17-3` in the blueprint. -/
theorem regroup_line_answer_sum_at {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (first second : Placement)
    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    (G : Option (PauliScalar P) → Option (PauliScalar P) →
      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side)) :
    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
        stateQForm S.psiHat
          ((S.placedMeasurement first
            ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
            S.place second (G o.1 o.2))) =
      ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
        (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
          S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) := by
  classical
  have hsum : ∀ (s : Finset (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)))
      (M : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
        Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))
      (N : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)),
      stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place first (∑ fs ∈ s, M fs) * N) =
        ∑ fs ∈ s, stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place first (M fs) * N) := by
    intro s M N
    rw [S.place_finsetSum]
    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, Finset.sum_mul]
  calc
    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
          stateQForm S.psiHat
            ((S.placedMeasurement first
              ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
                (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
              S.place second (G o.1 o.2))) =
        ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
          ∑ fs ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun fs =>
              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2) = o),
            stateQForm S.psiHat
              (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
                S.place second (G o.1 o.2)) := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ => ?_
      rw [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect,
        MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
      exact hsum _ _ _
    _ = ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
          ∑ fs ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun fs =>
              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2) = o),
            stateQForm S.psiHat
              (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
                S.place second
                  (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))) := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ =>
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun fs hfs => ?_
      rw [← (Finset.mem_filter.mp hfs).2]
    _ = ∑ fs : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
          DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d),
          stateQForm S.psiHat
            (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
              S.place second
                (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))) :=
      Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to (fun fs _ => Finset.mem_univ _) _
    _ = ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
          (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
            S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) :=
      Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := fun fs => stateQForm S.psiHat
        (S.place first ((lines.T first.side lineX lineZ).effect fs) *
          S.place second (G (evalOpt lineX x fs.1) (evalOpt lineZ z fs.2))))

theorem regroup_line_answer_sum {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    (G : Option (PauliScalar P) → Option (PauliScalar P) →
      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
        stateQForm S.psiHat
          ((S.placedMeasurement .AA'
            ((lines.T .alice lineX lineZ).postprocess (fun fs =>
              (evalOpt lineX x fs.1, evalOpt lineZ z fs.2)))).effect o *
            S.place .BA'' (G o.1 o.2))) =
      ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
        (S.place .AA' ((lines.T .alice lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ)) *
          S.place .BA'' (G (evalOpt lineX x fX) (evalOpt lineZ z fZ))) := by
  exact regroup_line_answer_sum_at lines .AA' .BA'' lineX lineZ x z G

/-- The sub-line average of a function of the two source lines and the
`Z`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products
of two restricted line-point laws, the `Z`-point being the point of the second
factor.  This is the use of Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines` in the proof of
`lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
theorem SubLineWitness.exists_avgOver_Z_eq_mixture (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (sublines : SubLineWitness P)
    (F : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → ℝ) :
    ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P), components.IsProbability ∧
      avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
            (fun t => F (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
              (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
        avgOver components (fun c =>
          avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)

    rw [Distribution.avgOver_map, subLinePointDist, Distribution.avgOver_map,

  refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun c => ?_
  rw [subLineZComponentDist, Distribution.avgOver_map, Distribution.prod_map_left,

/-! ## The two one-point overlaps -/

section Overlaps

variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
  {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}

/-- The overlap of the paired-line measurement at two source lines with the
expanded `Z`-point effect at a point, summed over the line answers.  This is
the integrand of the left-hand side of `lem:claim-17-3`, as a function of the
two source lines and the `Z`-point alone. -/
def zPointOverlapAt (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (first second : Placement)
    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
    (S.place first ((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.1.2).effect (fX, fZ)) *
      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2).effect (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))

/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed overlap. -/
def zPointOverlap (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
    (S.place .AA' ((lines.T .alice w.1.1 w.1.2).effect (fX, fZ)) *
      S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z w.2).effect (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))

/-- At a pair of line-point pairs, the `Z`-point overlap is the overlap of the
evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed `Z`-point measurement; the
`X`-point of the first pair only labels the evaluation classes. -/
theorem zPointOverlap_eq_at (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (first second : Placement)
    (w : LinePointPairSample P) :
    zPointOverlapAt lines first second ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2) =
      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
        stateQForm S.psiHat
          (S.place first
            (((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
              (evalOpt w.1.1 w.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt w.2.1 w.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
            S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2.2).effect o.2)) :=
  (regroup_line_answer_sum_at lines first second w.1.1 w.2.1 w.1.2 w.2.2
    (fun _ o2 => (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2.2).effect o2)).symm

/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
theorem zPointOverlap_eq (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (w : LinePointPairSample P) :
    zPointOverlap lines ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2) =
      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
        stateQForm S.psiHat
          (S.place .AA'
            (((lines.T .alice w.1.1 w.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
              (evalOpt w.1.1 w.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt w.2.1 w.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
            S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z w.2.2).effect o.2)) := by
  exact zPointOverlap_eq_at lines .AA' .BA'' w

/-- The `Z`-point overlap is nonnegative. -/
theorem zPointOverlap_nonneg_at (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second)
    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) :
    0 ≤ zPointOverlapAt lines first second w :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun fX _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun fZ _ =>

      ((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.1.2).pos (fX, fZ))
      ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2).pos (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))

/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
theorem zPointOverlap_nonneg (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) :

theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_zPointOverlap_le_one_at (sublines : SubLineWitness P)

        (restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability P c.1 c.2.2))

theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_zPointOverlap_le_one (sublines : SubLineWitness P)
